answer: I'd like to talk about an event I still feel a little sad about missing. A time I sadly missed an important event was a close friend's wedding, which I had genuinely been looking forward to. He was one of my best friends from university, and the wedding was in Rajshahi about two years ago. Unfortunately, I [[came down with]] a high fever just a day before and was simply too unwell to travel. It was supposed to be the first time our whole university group had been together in years. I was absolutely [[devastated]], because I had promised to be there and had even helped with some of the preparations. Lying at home while the celebration went on without me was deeply [[frustrating]], especially when photos and videos kept arriving on my phone. I remember feeling guilty, even though the situation was entirely out of my control. My mother insisted I stay in bed, and of course she was right. My friend was incredibly understanding, which only made me feel worse about missing it. To make up for it, I visited them as soon as I recovered and gave them a [[heartfelt]] gift, a framed photo of our old university group. Honestly, the experience taught me how unpredictable life can be and how we cannot always control our circumstances. It also showed me the value of a [[forgiving]] friend. Although I still regret missing it, I have [[made peace with]] the fact that some things are simply beyond our control. My friend and his wife still joke that I owe them a dance.

followUps.q: Do you often go to weddings?
followUps.answer: Quite often, actually. Weddings in Bangladesh are big occasions, and between relatives, neighbours and friends, there always seems to be one coming up, especially in the winter season.

followUps.q: How did your friend react when you told him you couldn't come?
followUps.answer: He was very kind about it. He told me to rest and not to worry, and he even called me during the reception so I could say a few words to everyone.

note: Specified the friend and Rajshahi; illness softened to a high fever; plain mark 'understanding' replaced by 'came down with', 'heartfelt', 'made peace with'.
